title: Marcos, Lipton: No signing of Pax Silica during Trump's state visit
summary: President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr. and US Ambassador to the Philippines Lee Lipton said Wednesday that there will be no signing of the Pax Silica initiative during US President Donald Trump's…

blocks.text: President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr. and US Ambassador to the Philippines Lee Lipton said Wednesday that there will be no signing of the Pax Silica initiative during US President Donald Trump's state visit in the Philippines.
"No, not on this trip. We are not doing it. We are not covering that on this trip," Marcos said.

Announced in April, the Pax Silica initiative is a US-led effort to build a network of allied supply chains for critical technologies and minerals, which the Philippines will host in New Clark City in Tarlac.

Officials have clarified that there will be no data centers included in the Pax Silica initiative, as its main objective is to process the country’s minerals and make high-tech components for AI and semiconductors.

Trade Undersecretary and Board of Investments managing head Ceferino Rodolfo earlier said the legal framework for the proposed Pax Silica initiative is still expected to be signed by the Philippine and American governments before 2026 ends.
The US President's visit has drawn protests from various groups across the country, mainly due to the proposed Pax Silica initiative. —AOL, GMA News
